8.9.3. Generalized Packing Measures and Dimension Functions. We briefly discuss here the 'dual' notions, in some sense, of the (generalized) Hausdorff measure and Hausdorff dimension (function), namely, the (generalized) packing measure and dimension (function). These notions were first introduced by D. Sullivan in the late 1970s and early 1980s [ 576 -578 ] for topological, geometric group-theoretic, and dynamical systems reasons-as well as, independently, precisely defined and studied in the early-to-mid 1980s from an analytical, measure-theoretic, and probabilistic point of view by C. Tricot in [ 590 ] and by the latter author and S. J. Taylor in [ 585 ]. We choose here to present these notions in the simplest possible way because they are technically somewhat involved and, possibly, a little cumbersome. Just like the Hausdorff dimension (and unlike the Minkowski and box-counting dimension), the packing dimension-along with the associated 'modified box-counting dimension' -are usually very difficult to compute, in practice. However, they are rather useful theoretical tools.

One basic fact of the theory is that an arbitrary bounded subset 𝐴 of ℝ 𝑚 is 'fractal' (in the above sense) iff its closure (which is necessarily compact) is 'fractal'. Note that 𝐴 itself need not be Lebesgue measurable, and let alone Borel measurable. Consequently, even if 𝐴 is, for example, a bounded Lebesgue subset of ℝ 𝑚 which is not Borel measurable, it could be fractal in that sense (and necessarily, its closure 𝐴 , which is compact, would be fractal as well). It is an open problem whether there are any such fractal sets of geometric, analytic, or number-theoretic interest, but if we assume the Axiom of (Countable) Choice, it is natural to conjecture that it would indeed be the case.
